Hi Tom — thanks for the specifics. Quick responses and attaching the questionnaire to kick off the evidence collection:

1) SOC 2: Redwood has a SOC 2 Type II report (period: Jan–Dec 2025). I'll attach a redacted stub (cover + opinion) for initial review. We can provide the full report under an NDA/controlled access if needed.

2) Logs: our default production log retention is 90 days in a searchable index. Logs older than 90 days are archived in compressed storage for up to 365 days (12 months) and can be restored to a searchable state within 24 hours on request. For customers needing extended hot retention we offer configurable retention policies as part of Dedicated/Private plans (we can discuss SOW if Hearthwell needs >90 days hot storage).

3) Backups & snapshots: backups are database-level snapshots (logical + physical DB dumps depending on engine) and incremental object storage snapshots for model artifacts. We do not create full VM images for customer data as part of standard backups. Backups are retained for 180 days by default; longer retention (up to 12 months) can be requested and is configurable at contract time.

4) Deletion propagation: deletion requests (subject access erasure / legal takedown) are applied to the live store immediately; we also schedule purges in the backup retention lifecycle. For backups, we provide evidence of purge workflows and deletion logs; full permanent removal from immutable archives is governed by the configured retention window and legal holds.

I've attached: Vendor_Security_Questionnaire.xlsx (sheet 1 prefilled with our answers where applicable) and Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_2025.pdf (redacted stub).

- Tom: review the attached questionnaire and let us know which sections you want us to expand on (RPO/RTO, encryption/KMS details, access controls).

Hi Tom & team,

Adding a few technical clarifications on the backup/retention/deletion behavior to help with your review:

- Backup scope: Production backups capture customer-specific databases (logical dumps for Postgres/MySQL, filesystem snapshots for object stores containing customer payloads) and model artifact snapshots. We do not include host-level credentials in backups.

- Immutable storage & purge: Backups are stored in encrypted object storage with lifecycle policies. Backups marked for deletion enter a staged purge pipeline — deletion manifests are generated and applied within the retention job; for standard retention windows (180 days) purges are executed within 72 hours of the scheduled retention expiration.

- Deletion evidence: We maintain an audit trail for deletion operations that includes: request id, actor, timestamp, affected objects, and purge job id. We can produce CSV evidence for specific erasure requests and a summary report for SOC2 evidence packs.

- Log retention & search restore: Archived logs are compressed and moved to a lower-cost tier. On restore request we spin up a temporary indexer to rehydrate the relevant date range; typical restore time for a 30–90 day range is under 4 hours, and for a full 12-month range is within 24 hours depending on size.

- RPO/RTO: Default RPO is 1 hour for critical state (metadata + ingest checkpoints), RTO for a database-level restore from backup is typically 4–12 hours depending on dataset size. If you need strict RPO/RTO numbers we can add SLA-backed commitments under Dedicated/Private offers.

I'll add the above to the questionnaire where appropriate. If you have a legal hold requirement, please flag it now so we avoid retention purges for that data.

Thanks,
